title: Business analysis report
cover_note: Every figure in this report comes from the stored results of the analysis run named above: SQL and statistical models that ran on your data. Nothing was estimated or written by an AI model. What-if scenarios are not included.
engine_note: Finding titles and notes are written by the analysis engine in English.
summary_intro: The findings with the largest estimated business impact, highest first.
no_findings: The analysis produced no findings for this file.
low_flag: Low confidence: treat as an early signal, not a conclusion.
kpis_intro: The dashboard's default view: the last 90 days of data ({start} to {end}) compared with the 90 days before ({prev_start} to {prev_end}).
trend_intro: Net revenue per {unit} with the forecast of the next periods. The darker band is the 80% range, the lighter band the 95% range.
trend_baseline: The forecast model did not beat the simple seasonal baseline in back-tests, so treat it with care.
contributors_intro: Positive sales only, over the whole file. A items make up the first 80% of sales, B items the next 15%, C items the rest.
dead_stock_text: {count} of {total} products had no sales in the {days} days up to {as_of}.
unusual_intro: Periods where net revenue was far from its usual level. {total} were found; the {shown} largest are listed by date.
segments_intro: {customers} customers grouped by how recently, how often and how much they buy. Actions are suggestions, not tested results.
churn_intro: {scored} customers were scored for the chance they stop buying within {window} days. Only totals are shown; no customer is named.
churn_rank_note: Probabilities were not reliable enough, so customers are ranked instead; the top 10% are the highest-ranked tenth.
assumptions: Revenue is net of returns and refunds. Periods without sales count as zero. Forecast ranges are the ranges of the chosen model, checked on past data. Associations are not causes.
appendix_intro: The exact queries behind each finding and how many rows each returned.
